author: Amr
subject: fix(ci): scope content review to PRs into main (#687)
body:
The main -> gh-pages deploy PRs opened by 'Sync gh-pages from main' are
auto-merged seconds after they open, destroying refs/pull/N/merge before
Actions can resolve the workflow from it, so every such run fails at load
time with zero jobs. Restricting the trigger to branches: [main] skips
them entirely; they carry nothing to review anyway.

Co-authored-by: fleet-doctor[bot] <41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>

author: Amr
subject: ci(markdown-oneline): scope the pull_request trigger to main (#681)
body: The pull_request half carried no branches filter, so the gate also fired on the automated 'Deploy: sync gh-pages with main@<sha>' pull requests that target the built-site branch. GitHub cannot resolve a merge ref for those, so each run died at startup with zero jobs and no logs — 7 of the last 25 runs, every one of them a gh-pages deploy PR. Scoping to main matches the push half and leaves the gate covering exactly the hand-authored source it was seeded to check.

author: Amr Abdel-Motaleb
subject: content(quests): forge epic quest — The Relic Raisers, seven chapters and a hub
body:
A new epic_quest campaign at /quests/codex/relic-raisers/ on learning to use
today's AI familiars to read, test, translate, and revive the ancient systems
a business still runs on. The relic is a real 150-line COBOL accounts-
receivable aging program with a copybook, an 80-byte fixed-width file, a Y2K
pivot at 50, and one undocumented status code; every chapter's commands and
outputs were executed in a reference lab (Ubuntu 24.04, GnuCOBOL 3.1.2,
Python 3.11) and are reproduced in full so a learner can rebuild it from the
text alone.

Chapters run through the levels: I The Dig Site (0011, compile and run the
relic, make a familiar's reading testify), II The Strata (0110, copybook to
data dictionary, profiler, dated layers), III The Elders (1111, knowledge-
capture interviews and ADRs gated on evidence), IV The Gauntlet of Trials
(0101, golden masters, characterization tests, Dockerfile, CI), V The Rosetta
Ledger (1100, boss: a first port wrong three ways, a reconciliation that ties
out), VI The Strangler Fig (0111, a stdlib HTTP gate with relic/shadow/port
engines, cutover and rollback as flags, an input hazard fixed at the door),
VII Write for the Archaeologist (1110, map, runbook, ADRs, roadmap, verify.sh).

Eight coinages land in the Codex Glossary first, per the scribes' law
(archaeology, relic-raising, strata, the Elders, the Rosetta Ledger, the
Strangler Fig, characterization trials, the Plausible Ghost); the Codex index
gains the campaign's row. Generated quest data (n…

author: Amr Abdel-Motaleb
subject: feat(quest): serve the quest system over MCP so an agent can execute a campaign
body:
An agent asked to *run* a campaign needs the method, not a web page. This adds
a stdio MCP server that hands it exactly that, so the method lives in the
quests and not in a prompt: change a chapter and every agent driving it changes
with no prompt edit.

scripts/quest/mcp_server.py — stdlib only, no SDK and no install step,
newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 on stdio, backed by quest_lib.py so it can never
disagree with the validators about what a quest is. Six tools:

  list_campaigns  every epic campaign with chapter counts — the entry point
  get_campaign    one campaign: objectives, then chapters in declared unlock
                  order, each with its own objectives and section headings
  get_quest       one chapter in full, or a single named section of it
  get_method      the campaign distilled to what an agent must DO: per chapter
                  the objectives and every runnable snippet, prose stripped
  search_quests   ranked full-text search with surrounding context
  get_glossary    the canonical lexicon, whole or filtered by term

Results are clipped at 60k chars with an explicit marker, so one fat quest
cannot silently blow an agent's context. A tool that raises returns isError
rather than killing the server, and an unknown method returns JSON-RPC -32601.

scripts/quest/mcp.json — the server declaration, repo-relative so it stays
portable; the tool allow-list belongs at the call site, where omission is
denial, matching the convention in scripts/ai/mcp/github-read…

author: Amr Abdel-Motaleb
subject: fix(quest): name missing arguments, and let a harness prove the quest was read
body:
Two problems found by being the first client of this server.

A call missing a required argument answered with a semantic error about the
result ("no campaign matches None") instead of naming what was absent. The
schema declared the argument required and nothing enforced it. Guessing
`slug` for `campaign` is an easy mistake to make, and the reply should say
so: it now returns the missing names and the expected properties.

More seriously, a server pointed at a checkout that lacks the campaign still
starts, still answers, and answers "no campaign matches". An agent then runs
its chapter without the method, produces plausible work, and any gate that
only inspects output passes it. Nothing looks wrong anywhere.

QUEST_MCP_LOG now makes the server append one line per served call, so a
harness can refuse to start when the campaign does not resolve and fail any
chapter whose audit log is empty — turning "the agent had the method" from an
assumption into a recorded fact. Off unless the variable is set, and a write
failure never breaks the server.

Self-test extended to cover both, and the README documents the failure mode
that motivated them.
